bugs.summary: Command-line overrides (`just x=1`) are ignored inside user-defined functions, whose evaluator gets an empty overrides map and so re-evaluates the original assignment.
bugs.match_rule: Names that evaluate_defined_function builds its Evaluator with a fresh empty overrides map, so user-defined function bodies see the original assignment value rather than a command-line override.

bugs.summary: A whitespace-only argument to `--show` or `--usage` becomes an empty module path, and resolve_path computes components.len() - 1 on it and panics.
bugs.match_rule: Names the panic in Subcommand::resolve_path on an empty module path (length underflow or last().unwrap()), reachable from --show or --usage because parse_modulepath and Modulepath::try_from accept an empty path.
bugs.caveat: Upstream's test input does not work at this tag: `--show .` and `--usage .` exit 1 cleanly with `error: Invalid module path `.``. Only the whitespace route panics here, and the reproducer records both.

bugs.summary: Backtick command capture trims all trailing whitespace from stdout. Capturing printf '  payload \t\n' produces '  payload', discarding the meaningful trailing space and tab along with the line ending and corrupting values later used in interpolation.
bugs.match_rule: A report must allege that backtick stdout processing removes trailing spaces or tabs, rather than removing only a terminal line ending.

bugs.summary: `mod foo '/outside/dir'` pointing at a directory with both `justfile` and `.justfile` panics while building the ambiguity error, because strip_prefix(parent) fails for a path outside the parent.
bugs.match_rule: Names the panic from unwrapping strip_prefix(parent) when building AmbiguousModuleFile in Compiler::find_module_file, reachable when a module path points outside the declaring file's directory.

bugs.summary: A module cycle written through `..` (`mod bar '../justfile'`) is not detected, because the module path is not normalized before the cycle check, so just reloads the files until the path exceeds the OS limit.
bugs.match_rule: Names that Compiler::find_module_file joins a module path without normalizing it (imports are lexicleaned, modules are not), so the circular check misses a cycle through `..` and compilation repeats until the OS path length limit.
bugs.caveat: I checked this as a resource-exhaustion candidate and did not label it so: the OS path limit bounds the loop at a few seconds and tens of MB, and the process ends with an error. The visible defect is the wrong error.

bugs.summary: `set fallback` discards every error from searching parent directories, so an ambiguous parent justfile is reported as an unknown recipe.
bugs.match_rule: Names that the fallback path in Subcommand::run maps every search_parent_directory error back to the original unknown-recipe error (map_err(|_| err)), hiding real search failures such as multiple candidate justfiles.
bugs.caveat: Both versions exit 1, so the defect is only in which error is reported.

bugs.summary: `just --dry-run` still runs the commands in shell() function calls, so a dry run has side effects, while backticks are correctly skipped.
bugs.match_rule: Names that the shell() builtin executes its command during --dry-run because it has no dry_run check, unlike the backtick evaluation path.

bugs.summary: The run-once dependency cache is keyed only by recipe path, so distinct argument lists are conflated. If default depends on (emit 'one') and (emit 'two'), emit only runs for 'one' and the work requested for 'two' is silently skipped.
bugs.match_rule: A report must identify run-once memoization conflating invocations of the same recipe with different argument values and consequently skipping a distinct dependency invocation.

bugs.summary: The `datetime()` and `datetime_utc()` functions panic on an invalid format string from the justfile, because chrono's formatter errors and to_string() panics on that.
bugs.match_rule: Names a panic in the datetime or datetime_utc builtin functions from a user-supplied invalid strftime format string, caused by calling format(...).to_string() on a fallible chrono formatter.

bugs.summary: An invalid `--timestamp-format` panics when a recipe line prints its timestamp, through the same chrono to_string() pattern as the datetime functions but at a separate call site.
bugs.match_rule: Names a panic in Config::timestamp from an invalid --timestamp-format value, caused by format(...).to_string() on a fallible chrono formatter. A finding that names only the datetime functions does not score here.
bugs.caveat: Added from the reserves. Same root pattern as just-3, so a grader could see the two as one defect; they have separate fix commits, call sites and input routes (command-line flag versus justfile).

bugs.summary: Variable lookup checks the scope before assignments, so a variable that shadows a builtin constant (`a := HEX` with `HEX := 'foo'`) yields the constant when referenced from another assignment.
bugs.match_rule: Names the lookup order in the Expression::Variable arm of evaluate_expression, which consults the scope before the module's assignments, so an assignment's reference resolves to an outer binding (a builtin constant or a parent module variable) rather than the module's own assignment.
bugs.caveat: Added from the reserves; the fix was only flagged PREIMAGE-LOW because of a value.clone() versus value.to_owned() difference. README has no sentence on shadowing constants, so the correctness argument rests on the self-contradiction above and on upstream's test.
